summary: Turn 15. Map v5 was accepted and Candidate 2347fc91e49249aa8fca5330bbed6102 (the durable-metadata ballot overwrite) is active, so this turn moves it toward a deterministic observation with a construction exploration. The harness (draft file explore_durable_meta_test.go, execution_package ./epaxos) is an internal package-epaxos Go test that builds a minimal replica with Durable=true and an os.Pipe as StableStore, calls recordInstanceMetadata on an instance with bal=7 and vbal=2, and prints CA_EVENT JSON giving the record length, the first four bytes, the status and seq fields, and the boolean comparisons field0_4==bal and field0_4==vbal — so the clean-copy output will show which value actually occupies the bal slot. It touches no filesystem and no network. Submitted action=explore with the question 'which value does the record carry in its first four bytes, bal or vbal?', plus feedback referencing the candidate, B-DURABLE-META and F-DURABLE-META. The feedback states explicitly that this is exploration construction knowledge, not property Evidence: the exploration shows what the implementation writes for one fixed input, whereas a formal check would still need a separately fixed artifact and a grounded requirement that the durable record must round-trip bal. Remaining keeps the open premises: record the observed bytes, whether a requirement exists that bal be persisted separately, whether any restart reader consumes the record (none found in the captured files), and the still-unexecuted A1 fast path, A2 authority transitions and unread A4 membership. Preflight validation returns valid=true; formal acceptance and execution remain the controller's.
